title: Decomposing Numbers to 10: Number Bonds and Making 10
seo_title: Kindergarten Decomposing numbers to 10 Worksheets: Free Math with Pictures and Answers (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Decomposition of numbers to 10: decomposing and recomposing quantities to 10, benchmarks of 5 and 10, making 10, part-part-whole thinking
meta_desc: Free Kindergarten math worksheets on decomposing numbers to 10 for the BC curriculum: number bonds, hidden parts, making 10 on a ten frame, the benchmarks 5 and 10, and part-part-whole stories. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: A number can be broken into two parts that join back to make it.
key_sub: 7 is 5 and 2. On a ten frame, the empty boxes show how many more make 10.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A number can be broken into two parts: 7 is 5 and 2, or 4 and 3.
  • The two parts join back to make the whole.
  • On a ten frame, the empty boxes show how many more make 10.
  • Use 5 and 10 as helpers: 8 is 5 and 3, and 8 is 2 less than 10.

Examples

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Giving the whole instead of the missing partAsk: what joins with the part I see to make the whole?
Adding the two numbers shownIf the whole is given, the missing part is smaller than the whole.
Counting the dots instead of the empty boxesTo make 10, count the empty boxes.

faq.a: Breaking a number into parts, such as 7 into 4 and 3. Putting the parts back together is recomposing.
Seeing that a whole is made of two parts. If you know the whole and one part, you can find the other part.
They are benchmarks. Children see numbers like 7 as 5 and 2, or 3 less than 10, which makes adding and taking away easier later.

faq.q: How can I practise making 10 at home?
faq.a: Use 10 fingers or 10 small toys. Hide some and ask how many are hidden.
